title: Being locally of finite type descends along fpqc coverings (Stacks 02KX)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For $i\in I$ let $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ be the base change of $f$ along $g_i$, the second projection of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f_i$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] for every $i\in I$, then $f$ is locally of finite type.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KX (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-type, line 5737: 'The property P(f) = "f is locally of finite type" is fpqc local on the base'), the direction 'each base change $X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ has the property $\Rightarrow$ $f$ has it' of 'fpqc local on the base', Descent, Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310)

proof.text: Local finite type is Zariski local on the target (including invariance under isomorphisms), and stable under arbitrary base change, hence under flat base change. Use the Mathlib instances IsZariskiLocalAtTarget and locallyOfFiniteType_isStableUnderBaseChange. These supply locality and hflat for fpqc_local_on_base_criterion.

For a flat surjective morphism g:T -> S between affine schemes, g is affine and therefore quasi-compact. Apply the local-finite-type clause of lem-galois-lft-formally-unramified-single-fpqc-descent (Mathlib LocalFlatDescent, lines 35-36) via MorphismProperty.of_pullback_snd_of_descendsAlong to the assumed local finite type of pullback.snd f g. This proves the affine descent condition without repeating the tensor-product argument already formalized in Mathlib.

Apply fpqc_local_on_base_criterion to P = LocallyOfFiniteType, the flat-base-change and affine-descent verifications above, f, g, hcover, and the given local-finite-type hypotheses for all base changes. It yields LocallyOfFiniteType f.
